title: Double Dutchwich (Bootleg DFM)
author: ThePedallingPianist
rules:
This is my response to Scojo's setting prompt from 31st October, for which Flinty asked setters to revisit rulesets that appeared relatively early in his epic Dutch Flat Mates series to see if any more potential can be squeeze out of them now that Dutch Flat Mates has become a more mainstream and better-understood genre.
Many thanks to PrissyP and sanabas for testing.

I arbitrarily chose a puzzle that appeared on my birthday, which just happened to feature a ruleset I've not come across much before: Double Sandwich Sums. Given that the sandwich crusts are 1, 5 and 9, this ruleset seems to have lots of synergy with Dutch Flat Mates. However, while Flinty's original puzzle was perfectly approachable and fun, the nature of the ruleset created a bit of a feeling of two separate puzzles after a certain point: one to resolve the 1s, 5s and 9s; and another to resolve the other digits.

This isn't necessarily a bad thing, but I wanted to try twisting the rules a little to sustain the interaction between all nine digits for as long as possible, and the following puzzle is the result. It is, admittedly, far more difficult than the original, and so if the point was simply to remake and refine the original, I may have missed it, but what would a ThePedallingPianist puzzle be without a bit of extra difficulty crammed into it?! Good luck!

Sudoku: Normal Sudoku rules apply.

Dutch Flats: Every 5 in the grid must have a '1' directly above it or a '9' directly below it. It may have both, but it doesn't need both.

Double Sandwich Differences: The digits 1, 5, and 9 are crusts. An outside clue shows the absolute difference between the sum of the first two crusts seen from the direction of the clue in that row/column and the sum of the digits sandwiched between them.

For example, a row of 257619834 could have a clue of 7 on the left: (7+6)-(5+1); and 10 on the right: (1+9)-(0).
